Source. The outer HMAC executor reads the next attacker-controlled chunk from the parent `Datasource` and stores it as `operation::HMAC::modifier`. For the exact staged witness, this chunk is the 6-byte blob `20 20 20 20 20 20`.

The module reinterprets the attacker-controlled modifier bytes as a fresh length-prefixed `Datasource`. This `ds` object carries the shared read cursor that both the backend selector and `CTX_Copier` later consult.

The first modifier parse consumes the first 4 bytes `20 20 20 20` as a `Datasource` size header, clamps that header to one byte for `Get<bool>()`, and then reads the fifth byte `0x20`. Because `0x20` is even, `Get<bool>()` returns `false`, so `useEVP` becomes false and execution takes the `OpHMAC_HMAC(op, ds)` path. After this read, exactly one modifier byte remains unread in `ds`.

Inside `CF_HMAC_CTX ctx(ds)` at `module.cpp:214`, `newCTX()` reaches this allocator and returns a raw `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` heap object with uninitialized `type`, `hmac`, `save_ipad`, and `save_opad` fields. No `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_Init()` or `wolfSSL_HMAC_Init_ex()` has run on this source context yet.

The first `ctx.GetPtr()` happens while evaluating `HMAC_CTX_reset(ctx.GetPtr())` at `module.cpp:221`, before line 223 `HMAC_Init_ex(...)` can initialize the source context from step 4. Only one modifier byte is left at this point, so `ds.Get<bool>()` cannot even read the 4-byte length header it expects and throws `OutOfData`; the catch block preserves the default `doCopyCTX = true`, so `CTX_Copier` allocates `tmpCtx` and calls `copyCTX(tmpCtx, ctx)` on the never-initialized source object.

The copy helper now treats the raw source context from step 4 as initialized state: it reads `src->type`, copies `src->hmac.ipad/opad` into the destination's saved pads, and forwards `&src->hmac` into `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()`. This propagates the poisoned source `Hmac` fields into the vulnerable wolfSSL helper recorded in the MSAN stack.

Sink. `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()` reads `src->heap` and then branches on `src->macType` from the uninitialized `src->hmac` passed in step 6. Because step 4 never initialized that source object, MSAN reports a use-of-uninitialized-value at this switch.
